A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same research work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron-deactivation, steering, sensitivity, and cross-dataset transfer results for three audio-language models in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional cross-emotion transfer entries in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 substantially redefines MAD: v1 uses signed differences in mean positive activation against other emotions; v2 uses absolute deviations of firing probability from the all-emotion mean. This removes magnitude information and admits unusually low-firing neurons. CAS, renamed ConAct, also changes nonpreferred-emotion scores from negative infinity to zero. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use IEMOCAP, MELD, and MSP-Podcast, their existing emotion categories, and all six cross-dataset transfer directions. Additional Figure 5 cells expand reporting within these retained comparisons without establishing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator roster remains RND, LAP, LAPE, MAD, and CAS/ConAct, with the same three agnostic injection strategies. Within this retained roster, MAD's stated procedure changes substantially, and CAS/ConAct receives a revised nonpreferred-emotion score.

E3.justification: Table 4 sample counts, class-balanced evaluation, intervention-budget and steering-strength sweeps, randomized answer-option mappings, and 20-token greedy decoding are retained. The additional transfer cells do not document changed splits, metrics, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: The transfer analysis gains evidence involving nonshared emotion categories: four IEMOCAP-related matrices expand from four-by-four to five-by-five emotion cells, exposing Frustration and Surprise cross-effects. Intervention-budget, identification-pool, steering-strength, and layer-locality analyses otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions average RND results over five independent random masks. This disclosure moves from v1 Appendix A.1 to v2 Section 3.1. No new uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-run practices are reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Tables 5–10 retain their numerical entries, and v1 Table 11 becomes v2 Table 2 unchanged. Figure 5 adds transfer outcomes, including a -12.0-point MSP-Podcast Sadness change under IEMOCAP-derived Frustration masks. The separate macro-averaged injection summary in v1 Table 2 is removed.

T1.justification: The formal MAD definition changes from a signed activation-magnitude contrast to an absolute firing-probability deviation; the contrastive selector's nonpreferred score also changes. These are localized mathematical revisions. The remaining intervention and injection equations are retained after renumbering, with no new proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now attribute effective selection to mean-deviation-based rather than magnitude-based criteria, reflecting the revised MAD definition. The main claims about causal emotion sensitivity, targeted controllability, modest identification-data requirements, and partial transfer remain.

C2.justification: Interpretations of inter-emotion interference, strength–specificity tradeoffs, and Neutral's dataset dependence remain. Limitations concerning decoder gates, SER-only evaluation, and the absence of a causal interaction decomposition are also retained.

D1.justification: Model-source URLs, identification-pool information, prompts, answer parsing, and decoding details are retained. Reproducibility material moves from Appendix B to A, while existing RND and LAPE explanations move into the main methods section.

R1.justification: Genuine additions include Antverg and Belinkov (2022), AlKhamissi et al. (2025), and Zhao et al. (2026b), alongside further speech-emotion references. Neo et al. (2025) is removed, and the MSP-Podcast reference is replaced. Numerous other changes merely update publication metadata; the principal research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized wording and terminology edits, incorporates existing selector explanations into Section 3.1, and reorganizes the reproducibility and injection appendices. Most narrative paragraphs and the main section sequence remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially reorganized. The compact injection summary is replaced by the full dataset-by-strength table formerly in the appendix; v1 Figures 5 and 6 become one six-panel Figure 5 with expanded matrices. Heatmaps throughout receive revised labels and angled ticks, accompanied by substantial figure and table relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 makes detailed injection results and all six transfer directions easier to inspect and adds useful nonshared-emotion cross-effects. However, it substantially redefines MAD while retaining its reported scores and plots. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects the earlier description or changes the evaluated procedure, leaving the quality implications of the central methodological revision uncertain.
